extracted.intended_audience: H-1B petitioning employers, immigration attorneys, HR professionals, and stakeholders commenting on/implementing H-1B cap selection rules
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory guidance and standards governing the H-1B beneficiary‑centric, wage‑weighted registration and petition process, including integrity safeguards, registration/petition matching requirements, and how USCIS will treat gaming, related entities, wage levels, SOC codes, and geographic issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple registrations grouped; lowest equivalent wage level used
rubrics_metrics.description: All registrations submitted on behalf of each unique individual will be identified and grouped together. If more than one registration is submitted for a beneficiary, USCIS will use the lowest equivalent wage level provided in any of the registrations submitted on that individual's behalf when determining the weight to be accorded to that beneficiary in the weighted selection process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The number of registrations submitted on an alien's behalf does not impact the chance of selection. This beneficiary-centric grouping prevents employers from increasing selection odds by submitting multiple registrations for the same individual.

rubrics_metrics.name: Valid registration must represent a bona fide job offer
rubrics_metrics.description: A bona fide job offer is one that exists as described on the registration and petition and in which the employer intends to employ the beneficiary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DHS is adding that 'a valid registration must represent a bona fide job offer' to the regulatory language (new 8 CFR 214.2(h)(10)(ii)). If the employer is submitting registrations for different individuals for the same job opportunity, those registrations do not represent a bona fide job offer; petitions filed based on these registrations would be subject to denial or revocation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Existing registration attestation requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: All registrants must certify that each registration represents a legitimate job offer and that all information submitted is complete, true, and correct, and that they have not colluded to unfairly increase a beneficiary's chance of selection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Through this rulemaking the registration attestation is updated to attest to a 'bona fide job offer.' If DHS discovers certifications are not true, DHS may deny or revoke the petition and pursue other appropriate action, including referral for investigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Related entity determination (use of established factors)
rubrics_metrics.description: The term 'related entity' is used as it has been understood and applied in the H-1B program (factors: familial ties, proximity, leadership structure).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USCIS will apply the term consistent with prior policy guidance (Matter of S‑Inc., Adopted Decision 2018–02). Proposed regulatory language referencing 'related entity' will be finalized without change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legitimate business need concept
rubrics_metrics.description: The concept of a 'legitimate business need' is not new and was previously explained in Matter of S‑Inc., Adopted Decision 2018–02.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DHS did not propose to amend 8 CFR 214.2(h)(2)(i)(G) and will not modify that provision; it relies on existing precedent rather than codifying a new definition in this rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Case‑specific integrity determination for attempts to 'unfairly increase the odds of selection'
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether an employer has attempted to unfairly increase the odds of selection is a case specific determination based on the facts in the record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USCIS will examine the registration, the original petition, and any subsequent petition to compare offered positions, SOC codes, locations, and wage levels, along with the totality of the circumstances. USCIS may scrutinize changes that lower the wage level after registration to determine if the original registration was bona fide.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition must match registration identifying and position information
rubrics_metrics.description: The petition must contain and be supported by the same identifying information and position information, including SOC code, provided in the selected registration and indicated on the LCA used to support the petition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See new 8 CFR 214.2(h)(8)(iii)(D)(1). USCIS may deny or revoke an H‑1B petition that does not meet these requirements. However, USCIS may, in its discretion, permit changes in area(s) of intended employment between registration and petition if consistent with a bona fide job offer at the time of registration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proffered wage requirement relative to OEWS wage level
rubrics_metrics.description: The petition must include a proffered wage that equals or exceeds the prevailing wage for the corresponding OEWS wage level in the registration for the SOC code in the area(s) of intended employment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USCIS may deny or revoke approval of a petition that does not meet this requirement. This links selection-weighting to the OEWS wage-level framework.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of intent to deny before denial under integrity provisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Before denying a petition under 8 CFR 214.2(h)(10)(iii) for attempts to unfairly increase odds of selection, the petitioner would be given notice of the issue(s) through a notice of intent to deny.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This follows existing regulation procedures to afford notice and opportunity to respond prior to denial.

rubrics_metrics.name: USCIS enforcement and fraud referrals
rubrics_metrics.description: Existing regulations allow USCIS to address fraud or misrepresentation in the registration, LCA, or petition process through denial or approval revocation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If DHS determines an employer submitted false attestations to subvert the weighted selection process, DHS may refer the individual or entity to appropriate Federal law enforcement agencies for investigation and further action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Weighted selection objective and balance
rubrics_metrics.description: The weighted selection process increases the chance of selection for beneficiaries who will be paid a wage that corresponds to a higher wage level while not excluding those at lower wage levels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DHS views this approach as striking a balance between favoring higher-paid, higher-skilled beneficiaries and maintaining opportunity for employers to secure H‑1B workers at all wage levels; it is preferred over both pure random lottery and pure salary-based selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: No guaranteed selection or blanket approvals by wage level
rubrics_metrics.description: USCIS declines to ensure 100% petition approval or guaranteed selection in the registration process for aliens at certain wage levels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USCIS does not adjudicate registrations for blanket approvals and will continue to adjudicate every petition to ensure eligibility; numerical caps and adjudication standards prevent guarantees of selection or approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection of pure salary-based allocation (use OEWS wage levels instead)
rubrics_metrics.description: DHS declines suggestions to select registrations purely based on the highest offered salaries and instead prioritizes based on the highest OEWS wage level that the proffered wage equals or exceeds for the relevant SOC code and area of intended employment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DHS reasons salary-only selection would unfairly favor certain professions, industries, or geographies and could be inconsistent with statute; OEWS wage levels better balance occupational and geographic variation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geographic differences handled via OEWS area of intended employment
rubrics_metrics.description: The final rule neutralizes geographic differences in salary amounts by taking into account the area of intended employment when weighting registrations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DHS declines national benchmarks, cost-of-living normalization, or statewide minima because OEWS wage levels already account for occupation and geographic variations and are updated annually by DOL.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid combining/weighting multiple subjective factors
rubrics_metrics.description: DHS will not incorporate complex adjustments (age, projected lifetime earnings, education/degree weighting, cost-of-living normalization, etc.) into the weighted selection because combining many factors would be overly complicated, unpredictable, and subjective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DHS prefers the OEWS wage level system because it is publicly accessible, updated annually, and administrable in an efficient and predictable way.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve some opportunity across all wage levels (no exclusion of levels I/II)
rubrics_metrics.description: DHS prefers a weighted selection process that does not effectively eliminate the odds of selection for wage levels I and II.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DHS considered alternatives to heavily favor level IV but concluded the finalized weighted approach increases chances for higher wage levels while maintaining opportunity across all levels; uses probability calculations and Monte Carlo simulation to show expected selection chances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not set DHS‑defined minimum salaries for each wage level; rely on DOL OEWS
rubrics_metrics.description: DHS declines suggestions to set minimum salaries for each wage level and will instead use OEWS wage levels set by DOL.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DHS lacks the expertise and resources to create and update a new prevailing wage system; OEWS is the appropriate existing source.

rubrics_metrics.name: SOC code selection must reflect the nature of the job; weight by six‑digit SOC + location
rubrics_metrics.description: Wage levels are based on the OEWS survey wage distribution for a specific occupation and location (six-digit SOC), with levels corresponding to OEWS percentiles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DHS declines proposals to map four-digit SOC families to the highest-paying six-digit occupation within the family because that would deviate from long-standing DOL prevailing wage guidance and could cause confusion; DHS believes existing provisions can detect and deter occupational misclassification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cap-exempt classifications unaffected by weighted selection
rubrics_metrics.description: H-1B petitions for aliens employed by, or with offers from, U.S. institutions of higher education, related nonprofit entities, nonprofit research organizations, or governmental research organizations are exempt from the H-1B cap.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many employers and aliens in certain industries (e.g., healthcare institutions of higher education) are cap-exempt and therefore not impacted by this rule.
